newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM says no change in policy toward Burma.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM says no change in policy toward Burma.

text.p: Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Tuesday there will be no change to Thailand's policy towards Burma despite recent unrest there.

"Our policies remain the same," Chavalit said at the Foreign Correspondents' Club when asked if student demonstrations and bombings in Burma would result in any change to Thailand's dealings with its neighbour.
"We follow constructive engagement. It is the same, there is no change," he said. "We understand they have problems, but they are internal problems. We will not touch internal problems."

Thailand and the other six nations in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations follow a policy of "constructive engagement" towards Burma, in the hope of sparking reform within the country, saying isolation is not the answer to Burma's problems.

Burma has been criticised by many Western nations for human rights abuses, and its failure to recognise the democratically-elected government of the National League for Democracy party led by Nobel Peace laureate Aung San Suu Kyi.
Thousands of students took to the streets in December in a series of demonstrations -- the largest anti-government protests since 1988.
Burma's military government has blamed Suu Kyi's party for being involved in and politicising the student protests.
